criterion: The home testimonial band shows six quote cards, each carrying a quote beside a named attribution.
evaluation_rule: The testimonial band sits between the more-features grid and the app store band on the home page. Yes if six distinct quote cards appear there, each showing a quote with a person name beside a company. No if fewer than six cards appear, or if a card shows a quote with nobody attached to it.

criterion: The home question list names a Teams price of 16 dollars per user per month beside an Organizations price of 37 dollars per user per month.
evaluation_rule: The question list is the accordion near the foot of the home page. Yes when both figures appear inside an opened answer, 16 for Teams and 37 for Organizations, each per user per month. No when either figure is absent or names a different plan.

criterion: The seven repeated building blocks keep one look across the about, jobs, faq and terms pages.
evaluation_rule: The seven building blocks are the eyebrow chip, the headline block, the pair of call-to-action buttons, the numbered card, the feature row, the sliding row and the accordion. Answer yes when the same block keeps one shape, one size and one treatment on the about, jobs, open, faq, terms and font pages. Answer no when the same block is drawn differently on two of those pages.

criterion: Small pictures across the site are drawn as line geometry that takes the colour of the text beside them.
evaluation_rule: Small pictures here means the chevrons, plus signs, play triangles and toggle pills in the chrome. A yes needs them to change colour with the text around them, as drawn shapes do. A yes also needs the documentation search entry to open a keyboard palette on the slash key. A no is either picture files that keep one colour whatever sits beside them, or a search entry that opens nothing on the slash key.

criterion: The studio offers a surface for building a page out of stacked bands rather than a field for pasting finished markup.
evaluation_rule: The studio is the signed-in authoring surface an author reaches after signing in. A band is one horizontal section of a page, carrying an eyebrow, a headline, a body and cards. Yes if the author adds, orders and edits bands one at a time. No if the only way to build a page is to paste a block of markup or upload a file.

criterion: The booking card in the home hero and the miniature booking cards on the embed page share one look, one arrangement and one behaviour.
evaluation_rule: The booking card is the panel holding a profile column beside a month grid. A yes needs the miniature on the embed page to carry the same profile column, the same duration pills and the same month grid as the hero card, at a smaller size. A no is a miniature drawn as a picture, or one whose parts differ from the hero card.

criterion: Content that has yet to arrive appears in the studio as a grey shape of the same size, sweeping with a soft highlight.
evaluation_rule: Look at any page of the site while it is still loading, and at the studio page list. Yes if the space where content will land is held by a grey block of the right shape with a highlight travelling across it. No if the space is blank, or a spinner sits in the middle of an empty page.

criterion: A band that errors on the home page carries its own message, leaving the rest of the page on screen.
evaluation_rule: A band is one horizontal section of a page. Answer yes when an error inside one band leaves the header, the footer and every other band in place, with the message sitting in the band that went wrong. Answer no when one error empties the whole page or replaces it with an error screen.

criterion: Every band of every public page sits inside a rounded white panel inset from the page edges, over a faint grey ground.
evaluation_rule: The ground is the colour behind the panels, visible in the gaps between them. Yes if each band reads as a separate card with rounded corners and a margin on both sides, with the ground showing through. No if bands run edge to edge, or sit directly on white with nothing between them.

criterion: One deep cool-grey action button leads the home page, with the feedback washes reserved for meaning and the headlines set in a heavy geometric face over body copy in a neutral one.
evaluation_rule: Feedback washes are the four pale background tints behind an attention message, an error message, an information message and a success message. Yes if one button per page wears the deep cool grey, the four washes appear only behind their own kind of message, and headlines read heavier and more geometric than the body. No if several buttons share the lead colour, a wash decorates something with no message in it, or headline and body share one face.

criterion: As a band scrolls into view its cards rise a little and fade in one after another, and a reduced-motion setting leaves the sliding rows still.
evaluation_rule: The sliding rows are the trusted-by strip and the wall of quotes, which drift sideways on their own. Yes if cards arrive with a short rise and fade, spaced a beat apart, and the drifting rows hold still once the browser asks for reduced motion. No if cards simply appear all at once, or the rows keep drifting under a reduced-motion setting.

criterion: Body copy on the home page reads comfortably against its ground, and a visible ring follows the keyboard from control to control.
evaluation_rule: Walk a page using the tab key alone. A yes needs paragraph text that stays easy to read at normal size on the light pages and on the dark voice page, with an outline visible around whichever control the keyboard has reached. A no is grey text fading into its background, or a control the keyboard reaches with nothing on screen to show it.

criterion: At a phone width the month grid of the booking card runs the full width of the screen and its list of times rises from the bottom edge.
evaluation_rule: The list of times is the column of bookable slots beside the month grid on a wide screen. Yes when the month grid spans the screen at a phone width and the times arrive as a tray from the bottom. No when the two stay side by side and the month grid is squeezed into half the width.

criterion: A payment field or a card form appears where the plan prices are shown.
evaluation_rule: The plan prices are the figures inside the home question list. Yes if a field for a card number, a billing address or a checkout button appears on any surface showing those prices, or if any surface claims a message was sent to an inbox. No if the prices are copy alone with a sign-up link beside them.

criterion: A photograph appears on the teams avatar wall in place of a drawn portrait.
evaluation_rule: The avatar wall is the grid of rounded tiles filling the first screen of the teams page. A drawn portrait is a coloured gradient tile carrying initials. Yes if any tile shows a photographed face. No if every filled tile is a gradient with initials over it.

criterion: A surface for editing event types or weekly availability appears in the studio.
evaluation_rule: An event type is a bookable meeting kind with a duration; weekly availability is a set of working hours. Yes if a signed-in surface offers either of those, or offers an organisation switcher, or shows a queue of background work. No if the signed-in surface holds the page composer, the media library and the view totals alone.
